rubric.result: Walked the seven sentences of `### Desired end state` against the sum of the nine commits. (1) 'Each sweep relays one dispatch for every checkout the registry holds': `harvest-clock.ts` gains the `relay: CheckoutRelayed` port and `#sweepCheckout` awaits `this.relay(root, checkout.repository)` after the harvest loop, once per surveyed checkout; `ct-api.ts` passes `relay: (root, repository) => relay.relay(root, repository)` into the one clock the runtime starts, whose `checkouts` is `checkouts.known()`. The qualifier 'a failed survey reaches no relay' is the plan's own Order decision, and the clock honours it by returning before the relay. (2) 'An open pull request frees the plugin's cap, so the next sweep starts the next admissible slice': `dispatch-relay-sweep.test.ts` builds the real `HarvestClock`, `DispatchRelay`, `StartMilestonePlan` and `GhDispatchCandidates` and doubles only `Gh` at argv level; with #10 at `status:in-review` and #20 ready, the dispatch is #20 — the plugin's own `collectInFlight` counts only `in-progress` (`plugin/scripts/dispatch.js`, `TOKEN_HOLDING_STATUSES` comment: 'CAP (collectInFlight) -> ... Only in-progress: a slice under review has no agent running'), so the freeing is the plugin's and the backend adds nothing. (3) 'A merge that a person makes on GitHub unblocks its dependants': the second case closes order 1 as `state_reason: COMPLETED` and leaves #31 with `merge-after #1`; I checked in `plugin/scripts/gh-issue-map.js` `buildDispatchInput` that deps travel in order space and are translated per epic into issue numbers before meeting `mergedIssues`, so the fixture genuinely exercises the merge, not an unknown dependency treated as met. (4) 'No caller names the issue': `MilestoneDispatched` takes `{repository, root, milestone}` and nothing else, the third sweep case asserts the recorded dispatch equals exactly that triple, and the gh double refuses any argv it does not know. (5) 'The relay derives the milestone from the frozen epic spec on disk, never from a stored phase': `DispatchRelay.#milestoneOf` returns null for a null spec, `!spec.isFrozen()` or a null `title()`, and `ct-api.ts` wires `spec: (root) => epicSpecs.mostRecent(root)`, which reads `docs/superpowers/specs` off the checkout; nothing stores a phase or a cursor. (6) 'The slice's panel shows its own stream and takes a message for its own conversation': `SliceSession.tsx` renders `<ImplementProgress issue root repo />` plus the labelled textarea and `Enviar`, and posts with the `agent` prop. (7) 'One endpoint carries that message, and the recorded conversation of that issue receives it': `slice-message-route.ts` builds `{agent, issue, repository, changes}` at the door and `ct-api.ts` hands the server `sliceMessage: (changed) => requestFixes.execute(new RequestFixesParams(changed))`, the same `RequestFixes` instance the pull request watcher uses, which calls `PlanAgents.fix`; `RunPlanAgents.#fixWatch` refuses a conversation that is not the record. Nothing a sentence promises is missing from the sum, and no promise an earlier commit produced is undone by a later one. Assumption 9 of the plan (a message during implementation refuses as `slice-message-not-delivered`) is the user's decision with follow-up #423, so I measured the narrower promise the plan made, not the wider reading of D-24.

Nine commits in `## Commits`, so the item has a subject. Read in order against every `**Objective:**` of §7. The sequence is additive: task 1 creates `dispatch-relay.ts`; task 2 adds the clock's port and the three trace expectations, adjusting the four pre-existing trace assertions of `harvest-clock.test.ts` to include the new `relay` step — an extension of the same trace, not a retraction of what those tests measured; task 3 adds only a test that drives tasks 1 and 2 through the real plugin selection; task 4 adds the route and registers its codes in the guard; task 5 wires both halves into `ct-api.ts` and updates the third and last `new HarvestClock(...)` call site (I grepped: the only three in the tree are `ct-api.ts:358`, `harvest-clock.test.ts:153` and the new sweep suite, all carrying `relay`); tasks 6 and 7 add the panel and mount it. The one reversal among the commits is task 7 replacing `<ImplementProgress>` with `<SliceSession>` in `Home.tsx` and dropping its import, which is exactly what task 7's objective asks for and which retires nothing — the panel renders the same progress section inside, and `ImplementHistory` and the coordinating drawer stay where they were. No scaffolding built for an intermediate state survives: the relay has one reporter (`RelayLine`), the clock adds no prose for it, and `requestFixes` is constructed once in `run` and shared by the pull request channel and the new endpoint instead of being solved twice. The ninth commit ('Hang slice-message-route.test.ts's POST helper off RunningApi') moves task 4's module-level helper into the class the yardstick requires and leaves task 4's four tests standing. One mid-sequence fact, measured and not reported as a finding because this run hands it to me as the plan's own defect already accepted by the coordinating session: at commit dd3d1553 `harvest-clock.ts` requires `relay` while its only production call site is task 5's, so task 2's declared `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` could not be green in isolation; the end state is coherent and the implementer refused to paper it over with a default that would have widened task 2's contract.

Measured `## Señal` — 'the next dispatch is recorded within one sweep of the pull request opening with no human input between' — against the accumulated diff and against /Users/jponzvan/git/control-tower-plugin/plugin/conventions/simplicity.md. Production code emits it: `dispatch-relay.ts` writes `RelayLine.dispatched(started)` = `relay: dispatched <repo>#<issue> as <agent>\n` on the success path of `relay()`, and `ct-api.ts` builds the relay with `stderr: (line) => process.stderr.write(line)`, so the line leaves the real entrypoint, not a test or a fixture; the same dispatch also lands in `PlanRecords` through `StartMilestonePlan`, which is what `/active-plans` serves to the page. 'Within one sweep' is the clock's own structure (`#sweepCheckout` relays once per checkout, `CtApi.#SECONDS_BETWEEN_SWEEPS`), and 'with no human input between' is what the sweep test proves by launching an agent with no caller naming the issue. With the repo's own instrumentation: the relay emits through the injected `stderr` port into `process.stderr`, the identical mechanism the sweep already uses beside it (`SweepLine.forSurvey`, `harvest #42: collected`) and that `ReviewWatch` uses; no dependency manifest changes anywhere in the diff, so no library arrives with this slice. Every label is bounded: the emission is one stderr line, not a metric with dimensions, and what it carries — repository, issue number, conversation — is the identity a reader needs to find the dispatched slice, in the shape `SweepLine` already writes issue numbers; no unbounded value is used as a dimension of an aggregate. The smell does not apply: the cell names something read in production after the merge — the `relay:` line in the API's stderr, which is also where the harvest lines a person already watches go, and `simplicity.md`'s 'who reads this, and where?' is answered by that same reader, who acts on it by knowing which slice the chain started without being asked — so the fact that `dispatch-relay-sweep.test.ts` asserts the exact line is instrumentation under test, which leaves the production lines in place.
